description:
User-requested follow-up from channel delivery review, 2026-11-20. Issue creation only; do not implement until requested.

Problem
Attachments.prepare_execution/3 currently collects all group indices, acquires all files and prepares every operation before Executor starts any upload. With 15 attachments grouped 5+5+5, a first-group failure under :abort occurs after resources were already spent materializing later groups.

Requested behavior
For upload_then_publish, process groups in original order: materialize group 1, prepare its upload batch(es), upload; then materialize/prepare/upload group 2; then group 3. Materialization remains execution-time work, never planning. The executor owns failure policy and decides whether to proceed; materialization is not a separate policy owner.
- :abort: stop after a materialization, preparation or upload failure; do not acquire or prepare later groups. Keep the publication barrier: no publication until the required uploads succeed.
- :continue: record per-attachment failures and proceed with usable files and later groups. Retain current upload-before-publication ordering and threaded publication behavior; this is not the earlier publish-ready-groups enhancement.
- Preparing a later group may now fail after earlier uploads succeeded. Under :abort, preserve those confirmed references as uploaded_only, publish nothing, and do not retry or delete uploads automatically.
- Example success with 15 files and assumed 5-file groups: acquire/prepare/upload 0..4, then 5..9, then 10..14; only then publish. Five is an example requirement, not the installed Mattermost adapter default.

Implementation investigation
Inspect lib/zaq/channels/delivery/attachments.ex, executor.ex, Plan/Step and existing bridge preparation/execution callbacks. Separate incremental group preparation from transport scheduling using existing boundaries. Handle multiple upload batches within a group, partial upload confirmations and preparation omissions without changing original indices, group identity or step dependencies. Keep authorization and actual-size/encoded-size checks before each affected transport operation. Preserve single acquisition for any attachment referenced by multiple steps; retain/release bytes according to remaining consumers rather than rematerializing shared records. Release bytes and prepared requests once no remaining operation needs them; reports/confirmation must retain only appropriate metadata and transport references.

Direct-send adapters
Inspect send_with_attachments (including SMTP) separately: there is no separate upload phase, and sending a group also publishes it. Specify the intended preparation/publication ordering before implementation. Do not silently introduce partial publication on a later preparation failure under :abort. Record the decision and obtain clarification if the requested group-local preparation cannot preserve that contract. The upload_then_publish behavior above is concrete; this boundary remains an explicit design question.

Action reuse assessment
Extend existing Attachments preparation helpers, Executor scheduling and bridge operations. No new Action, notification preflight, transport implementation or tool exposure is needed. Preserve trusted identity, selected-connector constraints, materialization authorization and NodeRouter boundaries.

Acceptance and tests
Prove ordering with observable acquisition/preparation/upload events, not just final reports. Cover 15 files in three groups, first-group and middle-group acquisition/preparation/upload failures under both policies, multiple upload batches, partial confirmations, original failure indices, shared references, no retry, uploaded_only accounting, and no early publication. Preserve first threaded answer confirmation, subsequent bounded reply concurrency, notices, root/edit promotion and confirmation stripping. Explicitly identify existing all-groups-prepared-before-upload assertions that must change; follow the repository test-behavior approval gate before modifying those expectations. Keep authorization, byte-limit and privacy assertions. Add focused property coverage for stop/no-later-acquisition and stable attachment accounting where appropriate.

Read AGENTS.md and applicable docs/agent-tools.md, WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, action-reuse.md, testing-approach.md, code-quality.md and services/channels.md; read documentation.md before updating diagrams/docs. Preserve other agents' changes. Run affected isolated suites and mix q. Update code-derived diagrams after implementation when authorized; final coverage/precommit remains zaq-1lw.13. No commit/push authorization.

comments.text: Investigation/plan: Attachments owns trusted acquisition, actual-size validation, bridge preparation and safe errors; Executor owns scheduling/failure policy, publication dependencies and reporting. Extend shared preparation helpers with group-scoped preparation, retaining prepare_execution/3 compatibility for direct-send and existing callers. Reuse JidoChatBridge.prepare_upload_request/2 and execute_delivery_step/3 unchanged; no Action/tool/transport additions. Cache original-index acquisition outcomes across groups; release source content, consumed upload requests and runtime bytes after their last consumer while retaining display metadata/references. Direct-send decision: preserve whole-plan preparation before any SMTP/direct send, including abort on later preparation failure; SMTP final continuation/header encoding checks remain unchanged. Tests first: new observable acquisition/preparation/upload ordering for 15 files, failure-policy matrix, multi-batch/partial confirmations, shared references, actual limits and stop/accounting properties; existing executor/policy/Jido/email/materialization suites retained. No existing assertion requiring all upload groups prepared first found so far; preserve early preparation error shape and existing payload assertions. No test behavior changes authorized or planned. Documentation: update Attachments moduledoc and channels execution contract; diagram reconciliation belongs to .12. Existing issue supplies this implementation step; .13 owns final coverage/precommit. No UI/E2E changes. Git initially clean; preserve concurrent edits. No commit/push.

Implementation progress: added new GroupExecutionTest and isolated support bridge; initial RED reproduced eager later-group acquisition. Group-scoped preparation reuses acquisition/size/bridge helpers; Executor now uploads groups in order before the unchanged publication scheduler. Preserve early raw preparation errors; later abort preparation errors return delivery reports with earlier uploaded_only references. Upload requests and source bytes released by remaining consumers; direct-send preparation barrier retained. Focused new tests 28 PASS, including first/middle failures across acquisition/upload preparation/message preparation/upload under both policies, 15-file ordering, multi-batch partials, shared success/failure acquisition cache, actual-size drift and stop/accounting property. Existing executor/policy checks previously 69 PASS. No existing test behavioral expectations changed. Broad affected suites running; initial foreground command hit tool 60-second limit without reported failures and was restarted detached. Required mix q running.

Completed in working tree. Upload-then-publish now acquires/prepares/uploads each fixed group before the next; Executor owns abort/continue and retains the publication barrier. Later abort preparation failures report earlier confirmed uploads as uploaded_only; no retry/deletion. Existing trusted materialization, original indices, actual/encoded limits, bridge operations, threaded root/edit promotion, notices and confirmation paths preserved. Shared original-index acquisition outcomes (success/failure) are cached once. Runtime source content, prepared upload requests and publication payloads are released after remaining consumers finish; reports retain metadata/references. Direct-send/SMTP decision: whole-plan preparation remains before first publication, with final SMTP body/header sizing unchanged. Existing-test gate: audit found no all-groups-prepared-before-upload assertion requiring migration; no existing tests/fixtures/assertions changed. New GroupExecutionTest covers observable 15-file ordering, first/middle failures under both policies, batches/partials, shared references, actual-size drift, direct-send barrier and stop/accounting property. Final affected validation PASS: 360 checks (18 properties, 342 tests), covering delivery, attachment policy, Jido, real Disk/SMTP journeys, confirmation, API, SMTP outgoing attachments/sender. mix q PASS (format/hooks/Credo/docs/compile), git diff --check PASS. Earlier malformed-record cleanup regression fixed and existing regression preserved. Service execution contract updated; diagram reconciliation remains .12; final coverage/precommit remains .13. No commit, push, staging or application Git publication.
